title: `TimeMarchesOn` won't be ran until media element starts playing or calls seek
body:
According to the spec, `TimeMarchesOn` would be run in different situations, and half of the places require that we should run `TimeMarchesOn` only when the media element's `show poster flag` is `false`. Ex. [add cue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#playing-the-media-resource:time-marches-on-2), [remove cue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#playing-the-media-resource:time-marches-on-3), [track mode changes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-model:time-marches-on), [startTime changes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-api:time-marches-on) and [endTime changes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-api:time-marches-on-2).

However, `show poster flag` would only be set to `false` in three places, which are [calling play](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#playing-the-media-resource:show-poster-flag), [autoplay](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#ready-states:show-poster-flag) and [seeking](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#seeking:show-poster-flag).

That means **"_Time Marches On_" is not possible to run if media doesn't start playing or has been seeked before**.

I checked some web platform tests and other vender's current implementation behavior, it seems that we would like to show cue (if cue's `startTime` is zero) even if the media hasn't started playing yet. In addition, according to the [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#seeking:time-marches-on), we will indeed show a cue after seeking, even if the media hasn't started playing, because we run `Time Marches On` after seeking completed.

Therefore, I assume that **we would like to show cues no matter media element is playing or pausing** and would like to propose we should run `TimeMarchesOn` in someplace without checking the `show poster flag`. Ex. run `TimeMarchesOn` when the media element's ready state reaches to `HAVE_CURRENT_DATA` or `HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`.
